<span id="finder-s-data-access-capabilities-overview"></span>
# Finder's Data Access Capabilities Overview

Data collection is the premise of all data analytics. The data collected will come from different sources, such as client side, website, Mini Program, etc. The data type is not only behavioral data, but also user data and device data. In reality, enterprises often face a problem, data is scattered in various departments, various systems, different business lines in the data database & table, and the criteria between the data sources and getting through the cost is huge.

DataFinder supports access to a variety of data sources, allowing enterprises to easily complete data link construction.

<img src="data:image/svg+xml;base64," />

 **(1) Supported data access methods**


---




* **Client side access**

   Support Android SDK, iOS SDK, Mini Program and other client side SDK access.

   <span>![图片](https://p9-arcosite.byteimg.com/tos-cn-i-goo7wpa0wc/56da04de0fe74c289ef296a1b96957df~tplv-goo7wpa0wc-image.image) </span>

   You can view the currently supported data sources in the Finder console on the **Data Management** \> **Data Transmission Service** \> **Data Access** page.

* **Server level access and import tools**:

   In addition to client side access, you can also complete data access through server level SDK, such as Java and Httpapi. For private deployment, you can also use import tools to complete data access, and import offline data, business database, third\-party data, historical data, etc. into Finder for overall data analytics.


 **(2) client side event tracking support classification**


---




* **Full event tracking:** 

   Open the switch can be collected through the standard SDK page browsing and button click data, optional on or off, the limitation is that the amount of data collected, can not be accurately analyzed, usually only look at PV and UV, and business related data is not recommended to take full event tracking.

* **Visual event tracking:** 

   Support visual manual circling on the page to set event tracking, which is convenient for business personnel without code foundation to use quickly. The disadvantage is that it relies on full event tracking, so full event tracking has limitations in visual event tracking.

* **Code event tracking (recommended):** 

   It is necessary for R & D engineers to manually write code for data reporting, such as business location event tracking. The advantage is that the code event tracking can be combined with the business design event tracking scheme, which can facilitate more flexible or business\-side analysis.


For more introduction of event tracking concepts, please refer to .

 **(3) Classification of user\-identified data**


---




* **Equipment data:** 

   It is used to uniquely identify a device, especially when the user is not logged into the app, so we can distinguish users by device.

* **Behavioral data:** 

   That is, event tracking data. In the operation flow of user interaction, the application finds key events for event tracking. When the user triggers a key event, the application will hand over the event tracking to AppLog, which collects the event tracking and reports it to the background.

* **User Data:** 

   When the user logs in to the account, or when the account is switched, or when the app collects other information about the user, the user information can be handed over to the AppLog, and the AppLog will be reported to the background for unified processing.


For more information on supporting user identity data, please refer to .

Data flow diagram

(1) Data is reported through various reporting methods (client side SDK/server level SDK/HTTP API, etc.), the first step of the data will go to the AppLog service, the second step will enter Kafka, the third step of the data is processed in a series of topics, and the fourth step is warehousing;

(2) When we query data in the system, it will query the warehouse data through the query engine and display it on the system interface.

<img src="data:image/svg+xml;base64," />

The above is an overview of the Finder's data access capabilities. Please refer to the detailed access operations of each end and the preset events and properties that are already supported [Preset Property Summary Table](https://docs.byteplus.com/docs/DataFinder/Preset_Property_Summary_Table) .

## Web JavaScript demo end\-to\-end demo

The following is a simple end\-to\-end operation demo of Web JS data access to demonstrate the detailed operation of data access.


1. Preparation for work.

   APPID and other information have been obtained with reference to the above.

2. SDK integration.

   1. Download and unpack the demo package for Web JavaScript, and use the power builder to open the sample HTML file in the demo package.

      <Attachment link="https://p9-arcosite.byteimg.com/tos-cn-i-goo7wpa0wc/83ac911d97884505bb52a40a5675a225~tplv-goo7wpa0wc-image.image" name="DataFinder JSdemo.html.zip">DataFinder JSdemo.html.zip</Attachment>
      

&nbsp;

      This example uses a simple page to collect and report user login and upload event\-related data as an example.

      <span>![图片](https://p9-arcosite.byteimg.com/tos-cn-i-goo7wpa0wc/a22cf00f104f4f5681ecc6ca4b14989e~tplv-goo7wpa0wc-image.image) </span>

   2. Introduce the SDK.

      Usually you need to copy the corresponding imported SDK code snippet and place it as high as possible in the HTML file tag.

      ```HTML
      <script>    
      //The function of this code is to cache the APIs called in the business code in the array q when the SDK main file is not loaded, and then take them out and execute them after the SDK main file is loaded.
      (function(win, export_obj) {
          win['LogAnalyticsObject'] = export_obj;
          if (!win[export_obj]) {
              var _collect = function() {
                  _collect.q.push(arguments);
              }
              _collect.q = _collect.q || [];
              win[export_obj] = _collect;                
          }
          win[export_obj].l = +new Date();
      })(window, 'collectEvent');
      </script>
      <script async src="https://lf3-data.volccdn.com/obj/data-static/log-sdk/collect/5.0/collect-rangers-v5.1.7.js"></script>
      ```
      

      The introduced code has been added to the sample HTML file. This step can be skipped.
